## ★★★ THESIS — THE CHANNEL INTO JAKE'S POSITION, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST CRACK-SUPPORTIVE ARGUMENT OF THE WEEK
- **★★★★★★ GAS-TO-OIL SWITCHING IS THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS A *DEMAND* CHANNEL THE US INVENTORY SERIES
  CANNOT SEE.** When European gas is scarce and dear, industrial heat and some power generation switch to
  **gasoil / fuel oil**. ⇒ **Incremental DISTILLATE demand — into a US market already measured BELOW the
  5-year low** (`oil-value-chain`, 8/18: 107,149 vs a 111,490 five-year low). ⇒ **This is a genuine
  reinforcement of the crack thesis and it arrives from a direction the vault was blind to.**
- **⭐⭐⭐ AND IT SUPPLIES A DIRECT TEST OF THE DISCONFIRMER FILED THIS MORNING.** The 8/18 fetch found US
  distillate rebuilding **~48% faster than the 5-yr seasonal norm** — the first real evidence against the
  position. **If Europe is genuinely short, US distillate EXPORTS should rise and arrest that build.**
  ⇒ 🚩🚩🚩 **FETCH: EIA weekly distillate EXPORTS (`WDIEXUS2`). That single series is the bridge between
  the European story and the US inventory data, and it either rescues or confirms this morning's
  disconfirmer.** **This is the highest-value unfetched item in the book right now.**
- **★★★ THE RHINE IS A DISTRIBUTION CONSTRAINT, NOT A SUPPLY ONE — AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS.** 10cm at Kaub
  with barges at 10-20% capacity **blocks moving gasoil UP-river into southern Germany and Switzerland.**
  ⇒ **Widens INLAND premiums while STRANDING product at ARA (Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp).** ⇒ **Acute
  regional scarcity AND coastal length, simultaneously.** **Unambiguous for regional spreads; ambiguous
  for the benchmark.** ⚠️ **Do not read "Rhine dry" as straightforwardly bullish the diesel crack.**
- **★★★ THE REINFORCING LOOP UBS ONLY HALF-STATES: the Rhine also constrains COAL barges → more gas burn
  → worse storage → higher gas → more gas-to-oil switching.** The river and the storage number are not
  two problems; they are one loop.
- **⛔ THE EL NIÑO LINE IS THE WEAKEST CLAIM IN THE POST AND MAY BE BACKWARDS.** European winter
  temperature is dominated by the **NAO / Atlantic blocking**, not ENSO; ENSO's European signal is weak,
  late-winter, and some literature associates El Niño with a **NEGATIVE late-winter NAO — i.e. COLDER
  northern Europe, not milder.** ⇒ **"Hope for El Niño" is not a hedge; it may be the wrong sign.**
  ⚠️ **Stated as a caution on the claim's confidence, not as a competing forecast — the vault has NO

### THE CALL (rule 14 shape)
- **1. THE MEDIA IS UNDER-WEIGHTING IT. Yes, measurably** — TTF at a 3.5-year high, ARA gasoil at a 5-year low, and US distillate exports at a 5-year high for the week got no lines in six inbounds on the day Brent hit $98.
- **2. JAKE IS NOT UNDER-WEIGHTING DIESEL — the book already IS that view, and today's series confirms it.** VLO 9 / MPC 9 / PSX 7 / PARR 8 are the European diesel shortage expressed through the one place it clears: US Gulf Coast conversion capacity exporting 1.7 mb/d of distillate. **Winter adds the heating-oil season (October pull) on top of a summer that already ran at record export rates.** The crack is the instrument; it is held.
- **3. ON LNG, THE PRICE SAYS "SMALLER THAN 2022," AND THE PRICE IS RIGHT ABOUT THE LEVEL AND WRONG ABOUT THE TIMING.** €73 is one-fifth of 2022 because the 2022 shock removed ~140 bcm/yr of Russian PIPELINE gas and Europe panic-filled from 75% to 95% by outbidding Asia; **the 2026 shock removes part of Qatar (~17% damaged + FM on the rest), Europe's Qatar share is smaller than its Russia share was, and US LNG export capacity is roughly double 2022's.** So the LEVEL is lower. **But Europe entered this fill season at 62% and is injecting BELOW norm at €73 — i.e. it is NOT chasing. The arithmetic (recall, ⬜ perimeters): ~100 bcm working capacity; 62% → ~83% (the relaxed target) needs ~21 bcm; at 2.1 bcm/wk × ~10 weeks to Nov 1 ≈ 21 bcm ⇒ lands ~80-85%, below the old 90%.** ⇒ **The event is not a shortage now. It is the OCTOBER-NOVEMBER FILL CHASE if storage tracks under target: that is when Europe starts outbidding Asia, TTF re-prices toward the spot-LNG level ($26 ≈ €80-85/MWh already) or above, and the demand destruction lands in SOUTH ASIA (Pakistan/Bangladesh/India refusing at $27) rather than in Europe.** Europe gets its gas by paying; the casualty is the buyer that cannot. **Jake is weighting the right thing and timing it early — the tell is the storage trajectory in October, not the September price.**
- **THE n:** TTF track n=3 points; export series 848 weeks; storage n=1 stale print. **Thin on the gas leg, deep on the diesel leg.**
- **THE DISCONFIRMERS, named:** (a) a mild winter — and the variable is NAO/SSW, not El Niño (`:L70-76`); (b) Qatar's force majeure lifting in November as stated; (c) European gas demand is structurally ~20% below 2019 (recall, ⬜) so the same bcm gap bites less industrially than it would have in 2022; (d) Chinese diesel export quotas rising into a Hormuz-shut market; (e) the Rhine — a distribution constraint that STRANDS product at ARA and is ambiguous for the benchmark (`:L62`).
- **⬜ WHAT CHANGES IT:** EU storage TODAY (GIE key — free; or Jake-side) and its weekly injection rate through October — the single series that decides "chase or no chase" · NWE diesel crack vs Sing (the differential rule) · pre-war Gulf diesel exports to Europe (Kuwait Al-Zour / UAE Ruwais, behind Hormuz) vs Saudi Red Sea volumes (Jazan/Yanbu, hit) · US distillate exports by destination (EIA monthly, to test that the record flow is going to Europe and not LatAm).
- **⛔ SELF-SCORE: THE VAULT WAS THE ONE UNDER-WEIGHTING IT.** This note said on 8/18 that the export series was "the highest-value unfetched item in the book" and that the TTF track was "still not built." **Neither was touched for three weeks; the fetch took one command.** The thread existed and was starved — the same failure class as rule 21, pointed at a series instead of a fact.
